newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Sabca sees stronger 1996 profits.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Sabca sees stronger 1996 profits.

text.p: Belgian aerospace company Societe Anonyme Belge de Constructions Aeronautiques (Sabca) said on Thursday it expected 1996 results to oustrip those of 1995 after first half profit jumped 26 percent.

"The results for the second half of 1996 are expected to be clearly higher than those of the first (half) and the results for whole exercise are consequently expected to be strongly up on those of 1995," Sabca said in a statement.
Sabca is 52.96 percent held by Dassault Belgique Aviation, a unit of France's Dassault Industries, and 42.80 percent held by bankrupt Dutch plane maker Fokker NV.
Sabca group net earnings for the whole of 1995 amounted to 128 million Belgian francs.
Sabca said on Thursday that non-consolidated, unaudited profit in the six-months to June 30, 1996, was 99 million francs, up from 79 million in the same 1995 period.

Sales slipped slightly to 4.00 billion Belgian francs from 4.26 billion. The company forecast full year sales of between 7.0 and 7.5 billion francs, down from 7.78 billion in 1995, which the company has earlier said was an exceptional year.
Sabca said a four billion franc contract to supply parts for fourteen Ariane 5 rockets had not been threatened by the explosion shortly after launch on June 5 of the first Ariane 5 spacecraft.
Fokker's bankruptcy in March had also not hit the company as hard as had been feared, Sabca said.
Sabca booked a 60 million franc provision in its 1995 accounts on a contract to supply Fokker wing parts.
It said, however, Fokker had been able to honour most of the contract. "This has as a corollary decreased the risks initially provided for," Sabca said.
Company officials were not immediately available to say if Sabca had written back some of the provision.

Sabca said, however, uncertainty over its shareholder structure continued. Fokker's administrators were continuing to look for a buyer for its 42.8 percent interest, while it was not yet clear what the impact would be from the planned merger between Aerospatiale and Dassault, Sabca said.
